articles.detail: 5 cycles, all completed; 11/7/9/10/11 stories selected against targets of 11/12/13/15/15; avg 9 published per cycle; 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active, and the pause gate (`noNewExperimentsUntil` 2026-11-05) bars a new one; nothing was evaluated or changed.
weakestArea: Science and tech together are 19% of output against 25%, down from 28% yesterday: science is 4 against 5 a day and tech 4, exactly on its daily target but under its per-cycle floor of 3 in four cycles (2, 0, 2, 0 after dedup). This is supply on a Sunday feed, not selection: the science items were mostly Scientific Reports manuscripts, and Ars Technica, The Register, The Decoder and 404 Media supplied no tech. Latin America has no dateline at all (0% against 5%), the second miss in a row.
watching: Saudi Arabia and Yemen: Riyadh airport was hit twice, with 12 dead and over 300 wounded reported, the Houthis declared all Saudi airports targets, and Yemeni forces neared Bab al-Mandeb.
Hormuz: Iran rejected the US reply, the Guards claimed a second tanker struck a mine, and US forces fired on a blockade runner.
Pakistan: Islamabad suspended Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's government, an appointed council took over, roads were sealed and Karachi banned gatherings.
India: the Delhi protest detentions went before a magistrate in defiance of a court order, and police sealed Dhruv Rathee's housing society.
Ukraine: Kyiv disputed Trump's energy truce and answered him on refinery strikes; EU foreign ministers meet on Monday.
Poland: a suspect was arrested over a plot against Tusk, and schools faced a third attack.
Lebanon: the death toll from Israeli attacks reached 4,387.
Nigeria: the electoral body dropped opposition candidates, and the petrol discount was extended.
Vatican: Pope Leo faces lung surgery.
coverageGaps: Latin America had no dateline; the AM region's 9 are the United States plus none from the south.
Oceania reads 0 in the region tally, though one science story is datelined Melbourne; the sixth region counted is a global (GL) tag, so named regions are five.
Four cycles ran short of target (7 of 12, 9 of 13, 10 of 15 and 11 of 15 selected) because the feeds held 5 to 9 multi-source stories and few usable niche items.
Tech was under its floor after dedup at 05:00 (2), 10:00 (0), 14:00 (2) and 18:00 (0), and three of the day's four tech stories are single-source.
Science was 0 of 2 at 10:00 and 14:00 and 1 of 2 at 18:00; Quanta, New Scientist, STAT, SciDev.Net and Carbon Brief supplied nothing, and two of the four science picks are thin.
Economy was under its floor at 10:00 (2), 14:00 (1) and 18:00 (2), and 7 of its 12 stories are the Gulf, Hormuz and Ukraine war filed as energy or shipping.
Politics is 53% of output for a second day (23 of 43).

Five stories rest on state media or advocacy outlets alone: the second tanker mine claim, the Lebanon toll, Iran's Riyadh-Sanaa offer, the Pentagon's revised war dead (RT) and the Korean ship's Arctic voyage.
Europe had 5 datelines, all Warsaw, Kyiv and Vatican City.
context: All five cycles completed, averaging 864s (selector 161s, writer 154s, editor 59s). The shortfalls are a weekend feed the selector declined to pad, as on Saturday; multi-source rose from 36% to 49% because what did clear the bar was mostly multi-source war and politics coverage. US datelines fell from 26% to 21%, inside target for the first time this week. No prediction-market row was offered to the writer in any cycle (`odds 0` in all five Indicators lines). The MercoPress addition to CURATED_SOURCES remains the first experiment to run once the gate lifts on 2026-11-05, and two straight days at 3% and 0% Latin America are the case for it.
